**LsRTDv1** is a reference transcript dataset (RTD) for lettuce, *Lactuca sativa*
cv. Saladin. It gives the lettuce community a transcript-level reference to quantify
against, so that RNA-seq analysis in this crop can resolve individual transcript
isoforms rather than collapsing them into whole-gene counts.

Alignment-free quantification is fast and precise, but it cannot be run without a
reference transcriptome — and the isoform-level annotation lettuce had before this
was thin. LsRTDv1 exists to remove that as a blocker.

## What is in it

LsRTDv1 combines long- and short-read sequencing with publicly available
transcriptome annotations, then filters the result to keep only transcripts with
high-confidence splice junctions and high-confidence transcriptional start and end
sites. The filtering is the part that matters: an RTD that keeps everything it
assembles inflates the isoform count with artefacts, and quantification against a
noisy reference is worse than not having one.

The dataset:

- raises the number of transcript isoforms per gene in the lettuce genome from
  **1.4 to 2.7**;
- identifies **novel genes**, most of them long non-coding RNAs;
- significantly increases the **mapping rate** of lettuce RNA-seq data.

## What it makes possible

Validated on a lettuce time-series experiment — mock-inoculated and inoculated with
the necrotrophic fungus *Botrytis cinerea* — LsRTDv1 enables:

- detection of genes that are **differentially alternatively spliced** in response to
  infection;
- **transcript-specific expression changes**, rather than a single number per gene.

Alternative splicing and post-transcriptional regulation during infection are largely
unresolved in this crop, and a transcript-level reference is the precondition for
studying them at all.

## Download

The dataset is deposited in **Dryad**:

::: {.publication}
[10.5061/dryad.xwdbrv1m8](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.xwdbrv1m8)
:::

| File | Contents | Size |
|------|----------|------|
| `lettuceRTDv1.fasta` | Transcript sequences | ~295 MB |
| `lettuceRTDv1.gtf` | Transcript coordinates and features | ~179 MB |
| `LettuceRTDv1_annotated.gtf` | Annotated transcript information | ~507 MB |
| `README.md` | Documentation | ~5 KB |

: Files in the current Dryad version. Read the `README.md` first — it documents
what each file contains. {tbl-colwidths="[32,48,20]"}

Reuse terms are stated on the Dryad record; check there before redistributing.

### Related data and code

- **Raw RNA sequencing data** — NCBI Sequence Read Archive, BioProject
  [PRJNA1018253](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJNA1018253)
- **Analysis code** — Zenodo,
  [10.5281/zenodo.11658411](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11658411)

## How to cite

Cite **the paper** if you are describing or building on the work:

::: {.publication}
Kara, M.F., Guo, W., Zhang, R. and Denby, K., 2024. LsRTDv1, a reference transcript
dataset for accurate transcript-specific expression analysis in lettuce.
*The Plant Journal*, 120(1), pp.370-386.
DOI: [10.1111/tpj.16978](https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.16978).
PMID: [39145419](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39145419/).
:::

Cite **the dataset** if you quantified against it — this is the citation Dryad
recommends, and the author order differs from the paper:

::: {.publication}
Denby, Katherine; Kara, Mehmet Fatih; Guo, Wenbin; Zhang, Runxuan (2024).
LsRTDv1: A reference transcript dataset for accurate transcript-specific expression
analysis in lettuce [Dataset]. *Dryad*.
DOI: [10.5061/dryad.xwdbrv1m8](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.xwdbrv1m8).
:::

Citing both is the safer habit — the paper explains how the resource was built and
what it is good for, the dataset DOI pins the exact version your numbers came from.
